bug_semantics: CVE-2026-16336/GHSA-rf2w-6p6m-3cqv claim CWE-601 open redirect by manipulating a redirect_uri argument in core/trino-main/src/main/java/io/trino/server/ExternalUriInfo.java. That argument does not exist: ExternalUriInfo only reads UriInfo plus optional X-Forwarded-Prefix and rewrites the path of the same-origin request URI. Trino OAuth endpoints have no client-supplied redirect_uri/callback query parameter. startOAuth2Challenge issues HTTP 303 to the configured identity-provider authorization URI (NimbusOAuth2Client.createAuthorizationRequest); the OAuth redirect_uri query string on that IdP URL is server-constructed from the request base URI (Web UI: request.getUriInfo().getBaseUri().resolve("/oauth2/callback"); CLI/token exchange: externalUriInfo.absolutePath("/oauth2/callback")). Authorization-code theft as described in issue 29754 additionally requires the IdP to accept an unregistered redirect_uri, which RFC 6749 forbids and which Trino docs require operators to register as the exact coordinator callback.
flaw_origin: False-positive VulDB CNA filing. CVE.org is PUBLISHED (assigner VulDB, not withdrawn/rejected) and GHSA-rf2w-6p6m-3cqv is an unreviewed NVD import with withdrawn_at null; NVD vulnStatus is Deferred, not disputed. The CNA text is a mis-description of unanswered GitHub issue https://github.com/trinodb/trino/issues/29754 (opened 2026-06-04, still open, zero comments, zero linked PRs). That issue is a defense-in-depth complaint that Trino does not pin a configured canonical OAuth callback, not a Trino open-redirect sink. No Trino commit after the issue changed OAuth callback construction or added a redirect_uri allowlist.

ExternalUriInfo.java (introduced 896545f6501227f78a5bdddd984cc2df6d008314 by Dain Sundstrom) stores X-Forwarded-Prefix and does uriInfo.getBaseUriBuilder().replacePath(forwardedPrefix); it cannot change scheme/host. Commit message: feature only enabled when http-server.process-forwarded is true.

OAuth2Service.startOAuth2Challenge (tag 481): Response.seeOther(request.getAuthorizationUri()) — 303 target is the configured IdP auth URL, not redirect_uri. NimbusOAuth2Client.createAuthorizationRequest puts callbackUri into AuthorizationRequest.redirectionURI only.

OAuth2WebUiAuthenticationFilter.startOAuth2Challenge uses request.getUriInfo().getBaseUri().resolve(CALLBACK_ENDPOINT) and does not use ExternalUriInfo for the challenge. OAuth2TokenExchangeResource.initiateTokenExchange uses externalUriInfo.absolutePath("/oauth2/callback").

docs/src/main/sphinx/security/oauth2.md: 'Set the callback/redirect URL to https://<trino-coordinator-domain-name>/oauth2/callback' when configuring the authorization server. RFC 6749 §3.1.2.3 requires the authorization server to match a registered redirection URI.

http-server.process-forwarded defaults false (docs/src/main/sphinx/admin/properties-http-server.md). Airlift RejectForwardedRequestCustomizer rejects any header whose name starts with 'x-forwarded-' with HTTP 406 unless process-forwarded is ACCEPT/true. Trino 481 depends on airlift 424, which includes that reject-by-default behavior (airlift#1183, 2024-06-05).

reasoning: Vulnerability-first review of CVE-2026-16336 against the assigned clone shows the advisory is factually wrong, not an unpatched Trino CWE-601. CVE.org remains PUBLISHED (VulDB CNA) and the GHSA is an unreviewed import with null withdrawn_at; NVD is Deferred. Vendor disposition is silence on still-open issue 29754, which is not a withdrawal, but the claimed mechanism does not exist in code. ExternalUriInfo has no redirect_uri argument; no OAuth resource accepts a redirect/callback query parameter. Trino's browser redirect on challenge start is to the configured IdP authorization endpoint. The OAuth redirect_uri value is derived from the request the client already made (Host/base URI, plus X-Forwarded-Prefix only as a path prefix). X-Forwarded-Host/Proto/Prefix cannot be injected in the default deployment because Airlift rejects x-forwarded-* unless operators opt in to http-server.process-forwarded behind a TLS-terminating proxy that is trusted to set those headers. The residual story in issue 29754 (IdP wildcard redirect_uri matching) is an authorization-server misconfiguration contrary to RFC 6749 and to Trino's own OAuth setup docs, not an open redirect implemented by Trino. No BIC or fix SHA is recorded because FALSE_POSITIVE does not require one; later history was still checked and contains no redirect_uri pin that would recharacterize this as a patched real bug.
